title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Carrying Out the Anti-Drug Comprehensive Governance Work of the People's Courts in 2010
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Seriously Carrying out the Comprehensive Drug Control Work of the People's Courts in 2010

Fa [2010] No. 149

To: the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Drug crimes require both temporary and permanent solutions, with the emphasis on permanent solutions. Carrying out comprehensive drug control in accordance with the law and continuously improving the comprehensive drug control system are of great significance for achieving sustained improvement in China's drug control situation. On February 22 of this year, the National Narcotics Control Commission issued the "2010 National Drug Control Publicity and Education Priorities," which set forth clear and specific requirements for drug control publicity and education work this year. The people's courts, in adjudicating drug crime cases in accordance with the law and vigorously carrying out comprehensive drug control work centered on trials, have important practical significance for expanding the social effect of trial work and maintaining social harmony and stability. To effectively implement the requirements of the National Narcotics Control Commission and increase the participation of the people's courts in comprehensive drug control, the following matters concerning the people's courts' comprehensive drug control work in 2010 are hereby notified:

1. Effectively Implement the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Severity and Severely Punish Serious Drug Crimes According to Law

Maintaining a high-pressure "strike-hard" posture against serious drug crimes is an important policy in drug control work and a policy consistently adhered to by people's courts in adjudicating drug crime cases. In 2009, the number of drug crime cases solved by public security organs nationwide, the number of criminal suspects apprehended, and the quantity of drugs seized all increased significantly compared to the same period, and a large number of major and serious drug crime cases were detected. At the beginning of this year, the Ministry of Public Security decided to launch a nationwide drug control strike-hard rectification campaign to further advance the people's war on drugs. In view of this, in order to form a joint force of judicial organs severely cracking down on serious drug crimes according to law and strive for a sustained improvement in China's drug control situation, people's courts at all levels must attach great importance to the trial of drug crime cases, continue to maintain the guiding ideology of imposing strict punishment on drug crimes as a whole, make full and effective use of penal weapons, and effectively combat, deter, and prevent drug crimes. People's courts in areas with a high incidence of drug cases must take effective measures to actively respond to the situation of a possible increase in the number of drug case filings, rationally allocate trial forces, and ensure that trials are conducted quickly and concluded promptly in accordance with the law while ensuring trial quality, so as to avoid case backlog. For major and serious drug cases with significant social impact, trials must be conducted quickly and concluded promptly, and the high-pressure posture of imposing severe punishment on serious drug crimes according to law must always be maintained.

In terms of policy understanding, the focus of punishment must be highlighted in accordance with the spirit of "Several Opinions on Implementing the Criminal Policy of Combining Leniency with Severity" issued by our court this year and the requirements of normative documents such as the "Summary of the Symposium on the Work of Trial of Drug Crime Cases by Some Courts Nationwide" issued in 2008 (hereinafter referred to as the "Dalian Meeting Summary"). Serious drug crimes and drug offenders with deep subjective malignancy, high personal danger, and serious harm, such as drug lords, professional drug offenders, repeat offenders, and recidivists, as well as drug offenders with other serious circumstances, must be severely punished according to law. For those whose crimes are extremely serious and who should be sentenced to death according to law, a death sentence must be firmly imposed according to law. At the same time, in accordance with the requirements of the criminal policy of combining leniency with severity, differentiated treatment must be adhered to, and a quantitative-only approach must be avoided. When sentencing, particularly when considering whether to impose the death penalty, various factors such as the quantity of drugs, the circumstances of the crime, the harmful consequences, the subjective malignancy of the defendant, personal dangerousness, and the local drug control situation must be comprehensively considered. For crimes with relatively minor circumstances and lesser social harm, or for defendants whose crimes are serious but who have statutory or discretionary circumstances for lenient punishment, or who have relatively minor subjective malignancy and lesser personal dangerousness, lenient punishment may be imposed according to law, in order to split and disintegrate criminal activities and give full play to the educational and reformative function of punishment.

2. Deeply Carry out Research on Drug Cases and Further Strengthen Trial Guidance

Conducting research and providing guidance on the trial of drug cases is an important foundational task for improving the level of drug case adjudication and ensuring trial quality. In recent years, people's courts at all levels, especially those in areas with a high incidence of drug cases, have continuously summarized trial experience and strengthened trial guidance and research, keeping the trial of drug crimes proactive. However, due to the continuous emergence of new situations and new problems in drug crimes, there are still issues in trials regarding the application of law and policy understanding that require in-depth study and resolution. To this end, people's courts at all levels must seriously study and analyze the situation and characteristics of local drug crime cases, especially in conjunction with the implementation of normative documents such as the Dalian Meeting Summary, continue to strengthen research efforts, and strive to resolve prominent issues arising in practice. Higher-level courts, especially high people's courts, must increase the intensity of trial guidance. While handling second-instance trials, they should further unify the application of law and policy understanding of drug crime cases within their jurisdiction by compiling and distributing typical cases, holding special meetings, and other means. For drug crime cases where the death penalty may be imposed, special attention must be paid to giving full effect to the role of "first instance as the foundation, second instance as the key." Procedures must be strict, standards must be raised, and for systemic issues in evidence collection, judicial suggestions must be promptly submitted to investigation and prosecution authorities, so that quality problems discovered in cases can be resolved as early as possible during the investigation, review for prosecution, and first-instance trial stages. For drug cases where the Supreme People's Court does not approve the death penalty, the relevant courts must carefully analyze the problems and their causes, and continuously improve the trial quality of drug death penalty cases.

3. Focus on Drug Control Publicity and Education, and Continuously Deepen Comprehensive Drug Control Work

In recent years, especially since the implementation of the Anti-Drug Law in 2008, people's courts at all levels have closely integrated trial work, stepped up publicity efforts, and carried out comprehensive drug control activities with rich content and diverse forms, achieving remarkable results. This year, special attention must be paid to the high incidence of drug cases. Taking the opportunity of trying major drug crime cases, activities such as live broadcasting of court hearings, public sentencing, printing and posting notices, and holding press conferences should be adopted. Television, radio, newspapers, the internet, and other news media should be fully utilized for publicity and reporting to expand the legal education effect of trial work. People's courts in areas with a high incidence of drug cases should, based on local drug control priorities and trial trends, concentrate on carrying out publicity activities for drug crime trials in April, June, and September respectively, and systematically link the year's focused publicity activities to form a strong momentum of people's courts severely punishing serious drug crimes according to law.

People's courts at all levels must continue to take the promotion of the Anti-Drug Law as an important part of drug control publicity work. Closely focusing on the publicity theme of "Drug Control According to Law, Building Harmony," publicity should be carried out in various forms such as producing display boards for streets, entering communities, and going into schools. Key periods such as relevant commemorative days should be fully utilized for publicity, especially the "June 1" Anniversary of the Implementation of the Anti-Drug Law, the "June 3" Anniversary of the Humen Opium Destruction, and the "June 26" International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking. Young people should be the key targets of drug control publicity and education. The intensity of drug control publicity and education for young people should be increased by organizing college, middle school, and primary school students to observe trials, holding legal lectures in schools, and appointing experienced judges as vice principals for legal affairs or off-campus counselors in middle and primary schools, so that they can more vividly understand the dangers of drugs and more consciously stay away from and resist drugs.

While carrying out the above drug control publicity work, people's courts at all levels must also pay attention to adopting other comprehensive governance measures. The Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Execution of Property Penalties" must be conscientiously implemented, the execution of property penalties must be effectively strengthened, so that offenders are duly punished financially, not only depriving them of the ability and conditions to re-offend, but also providing direct education to the general public, thereby better realizing the general preventive function of criminal punishment. For drug offenders who have committed relatively minor crimes or have less subjective malignancy and have been leniently dealt with according to law, measures such as return visits, assistance, and education should be taken, in coordination with penalty execution departments, for education and reform, so as to reduce recidivism. For areas where the manufacturing of new types of drugs such as ketamine and the participation of women and minors in drug trafficking are relatively concentrated, judicial suggestions for strengthening management and plugging loopholes should be promptly submitted to relevant departments and grassroots organizations to assist in preventive work. In addition, on the basis of past work, people's courts at all levels must actively explore new forms and new practices of comprehensive drug control, continuously enhance the scientific nature, targetedness, and effectiveness of their participation in comprehensive drug control work, and truly implement the work requirement of "social management innovation."

4. Strengthen Organization and Coordination to Ensure Greater Achievements in Comprehensive Drug Control

The high incidence of drug crimes not only directly harms the physical and mental health and family happiness of drug users, causing enormous economic losses to the state and the people, but also induces other crimes, spreads diseases, and creates a series of social problems. Facts have proven that drug abuse is often a major source of high crime rates and social instability in a country or region. Affected by a combination of domestic and international factors, China's drug control situation has always been relatively severe, major drug crimes still occur from time to time, and the task of comprehensive drug control remains very arduous. People's courts at all levels must fully understand the importance, long-term nature, and arduousness of further improving all aspects of comprehensive drug control work around case trials from the perspective of maintaining social harmony and stability and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and further enhance their sense of responsibility and urgency in carrying out comprehensive drug control work. People's courts in areas with a high incidence of drug cases must firmly establish the idea of making unremitting efforts, treat comprehensive drug control as a routine task of the people's courts, seriously organize and carefully arrange it, strengthen coordination and cooperation with relevant departments such as public security and procuratorial organs, establish a normalized comprehensive drug control work mechanism with rich content, diverse forms, and highlighted priorities, and constantly strive to improve work methods, strive for innovation, and ensure that comprehensive drug control work reaches a new level and achieves greater results this year.

All courts are requested to earnestly implement the above notice. New situations and new problems encountered in the trial of drug cases, as well as new forms and new practices explored in comprehensive drug control work, must be carefully summarized and promptly reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

April 6, 2010
